full_judgment: 6. Mr. Syed Motiul Islam the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the State submitted that the doctor who held post mortem examination found only two injuries on the person of the deceased and the ligature in the neck was found to be post-mortem in nature a that the doctor opined that death was due to shock and haemorrhage as a result of skull injury which is ante-mortem and homicidal in nature and this indicates that the deceased Sufia Begum was done to death and as she was living with her husband on the date of occurrence it can be presumed that the husband was responsible for the commission of murder. He further contends that by suggesting that the deceased committed suicide by hanging the appellant tried to save himself from being punished. As the wife was murdered while in custody of the husband the natural presumption is that the husband is the killer.
